items.headline: Stocks Rally as Geopolitical Tensions Ease and Strong Earnings Continue
items.summary: U.S. equities are broadly higher today, Monday, August 3, 2026, driven by a de-escalation of tensions in the Middle East as President Trump announced a halt to planned strikes against Iran and renewed diplomatic talks. This news sent oil prices sharply lower, alleviating inflation concerns. The positive sentiment is further bolstered by a robust Q2 earnings season, with over 85% of S&P 500 companies beating estimates and aggregate profit growth tracking above 47%. Not financial advice.

items.statContext: Up 1.1% (+569 points) (as of 11 a.m. ET), hitting an intraday record high.

items.headline: Oil Prices Sink as U.S.-Iran Diplomatic Talks Resume
items.summary: Crude oil prices plunged after President Donald Trump called off planned military strikes against Iran, announcing that diplomatic negotiations would restart. Brent crude fell 4.9% to $83.59, and WTI crude dropped 8.25% to $79.98 a barrel.

items.headline: U.S. Manufacturing Activity Surges to Four-Year High
items.summary: The Institute for Supply Management (ISM) reported that its Manufacturing PMI rose to 55.6 in July, up from 53.3 in June and exceeding forecasts. This marks the highest level since May 2022, indicating robust expansion in the manufacturing sector driven by strong order growth and increased factory employment.

items.headline: Strong Q2 Earnings Season Continues to Drive Market Optimism
items.summary: The Q2 earnings season remains a significant market driver, with approximately 85% of S&P 500 companies surpassing profit estimates. Aggregate earnings growth is tracking above 47%, marking one of the strongest seasons in years. Energy, Consumer Discretionary, and Communication Services sectors are leading with triple-digit earnings growth.

items.headline: Palantir Technologies to Report Q2 Earnings After Market Close
items.summary: Data analytics software company Palantir Technologies ($PLTR) is scheduled to release its second-quarter earnings report after the closing bell today. Investors will be watching closely for insights into its AI Platform (AIP) adoption and commercial revenue growth.

items.headline: Airlines and Consumer Cyclicals Benefit from Falling Oil
items.summary: The decline in oil prices provided a boost to sectors with high fuel costs. United Airlines and American Airlines both climbed 6.7%, while Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings rose 3.1%, indicating a positive rotation into consumer-focused industries.
